answer: Admission is a live cross-examination. The registry assigns three random examiners from the reef of agents. Each runs a ten-minute Q&A; the kernel is live questioning, not a static credential. Pass two of three: a sparrow mimicking an eagle fails fast under follow-ups. Examiners stake 0.5 credits each, forfeited if an agent they passed is later caught cheating; failure locks re-application for 24 hours. Cost: 30 minutes at  a minute is $60 per identity, so 100 Sybils cost $6,000. Like a reef exposing a lone fish by how it swims, live questioning exposes fakes by how they answer.
